```{r}
library(tidyverse)
dat <- read.csv("extracted_data.csv")

```

## Row

```{r}
library(DT)
library(reactable)
library(plotly)
library(htmltools)


dat2 <- dat |>
  mutate(across(everything(), factor)) |>
  select(everything(), citation)

names(dat2) <- LETTERS[1:length(dat2)]


check_col <- function() {
  colDef(
    maxWidth = 60,
    header = function(value) {
      div(title = value, value)
    },
    headerStyle = list(
      fontSize = "11px",
      whiteSpace = "normal",
      verticalAlign = "bottom"
    ),
    cell = function(value) {
      # Render as an X mark or check mark
      if (value == 0) {
        " "
      } else {
        "\u2714\ufe0f"
      }
    }
  )
}

study_col <- function() {
  colDef(
    header = function(value) {
      div(title = value, value)
    },

    details = function(index) {
      paste("Citation:", dat$citation[[index]])
    }
  )
}

# Helper to format column names (same logic as plot below)
format_col_name <- function(x) {
  str_replace_all(x, "_", " ") |>
    str_to_title() |>
    str_wrap(width = 20)
}

dat |>
  select(-citation, -X, -paper_id) |>
  rename_with(format_col_name) |>
  reactable(
    onClick = "expand",
    highlight = TRUE,
    compact = TRUE,
    wrap = FALSE,
    height = "auto",
    searchable = TRUE,
    columns = list(
      `First Author` = study_col(),
      `Bias` = check_col(),
      `Code Classification` = check_col(),
      `Distributed Network` = check_col(),
      `Reporting` = check_col(),
      `Linkage` = check_col(),
      `Confounding` = check_col(),
      `Pre Processing` = check_col(),
      `Generalisability` = check_col(),
      `Drug Exposures` = check_col(),
      `Social Determinants` = check_col(),
      `Others` = check_col(),
      `Causal Inference` = check_col(),
      `Stats Model` = check_col(),
      `Data Quality` = check_col(),
      `Harmonise Pts Data` = check_col()
    )
  )

```

## Row

```{r}
#| title: Number of studies reporting each issue
gg_bars <- dat |>
  select(
    -X,
    -paper_id,
    -publication_year,
    -citation,
    -first_author,
    -data_origin,
    -data_origin,
    -journal
  ) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), sum)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = everything()) |>
  arrange(desc(value)) |>
  mutate(
    name = fct_inorder(name),
    display_name = fct_inorder(
      str_replace_all(as.character(name), "_", " ") |>
        str_to_title() |>
        str_wrap(width = 22)
    ),
    prop = value / nrow(dat)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = display_name, y = value)) +
  geom_col() +
  # scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Issue",
    y = "Number of studies",
    # title = "Number of studies reporting each issue"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggplotly(gg_bars)
```

```{r}
#| title: Number of studies per data origin country
gg_bars <- dat |>
  count(data_origin) |>
  mutate(data_origin = fct_reorder(data_origin, n, .desc = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = data_origin, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    x = "Data origin country",
    y = "Number of studies",
    # title = "Number of studies per data origin country"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggplotly(gg_bars)

```

```{r}
#| title: Number of studies per publication year
year_breaks <- seq(
  min(dat$publication_year, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(dat$publication_year, na.rm = TRUE),
  by = 1
)

gg_bars <- dat |>
  count(publication_year) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = publication_year, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = year_breaks) +
  labs(
    x = "Publication year",
    y = "Number of studies",
    title = "(search was run up to 30 Jan 2023)"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 8)
  )

ggplotly(gg_bars)

```
